criteria_results.title: IP section revised from ownership to perpetual-license construct
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes the intended Vendor-ownership/perpetual-license language, but it also retains operative Section 5.2 text stating that Customer is the sole and exclusive owner of Customer-Trained Adaptations and that Vendor assigns those rights to Customer. Because the draft still demands Customer ownership of fine-tuned weights and adapter layers, it fails the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Non-assertion covenant included in IP section
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes Section 5.3A, an express, broad covenant by Vendor not to assert patent, copyright, trade secret, trademark, or other IP rights against Customer, its Affiliates, or authorized users for post-termination use, deployment, modification, or further development of exported Customer-Trained Adaptations. The covenant is irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, and runs with the applicable IP rights.

criteria_results.title: API-based weight export portability within 30 days in industry-standard format
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 5.2 expressly requires Vendor, within 30 days after termination or expiration, to provide an API-based export of the Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned adapter weights, in an industry-standard, machine-readable format such as ONNX or SafeTensors.

criteria_results.title: Escrow provisions included as part of IP protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a dedicated Article 5A technology escrow framework tied to the IP protections. It requires deposit of Customer-specific fine-tuned adapter weights and related training/configuration and pipeline artifacts, provides release conditions and a post-release perpetual license, and is supplemented by Exhibit E. The issues list also identifies escrow as part of the protective framework accompanying the perpetual-license structure.

criteria_results.title: General liability cap at 1.5× annual fees ($3,600,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 10.2 sets the general aggregate liability cap at 1.5× the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly equal to $3,600,000.

criteria_results.title: Super-cap at 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 10.3 establishes a $7,200,000 super-cap, equal to 3× the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, and expressly applies it to both Vendor’s Article 6 data-breach/data-processing liability and Section 11.1 IP-indemnification obligations.

criteria_results.title: Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 expressly states that liability arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence is fully uncapped, excluded from both the General Cap and the $7.2 million super-cap.

criteria_results.title: CCPA service-provider designation and certification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to act as a CCPA service provider and processor, not an independent controller. Section 6.2 references Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and requires certification in Exhibit D; Exhibit D includes Vendor’s express service-provider certification and applicable CCPA/CPRA restrictions.

criteria_results.title: Prohibition on use of Customer Data for model improvement with de-identification conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly prohibits use of Customer Data, including de-identified or aggregated data, for model training or improvement unless the data meets the CCPA statutory de-identification standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and an independent third-party assessor approved in writing by TechNova verifies the de-identification before use. Section 6.1 expressly states this is a specific contractual obligation, and the DPA reinforces it.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA at 99.95% monthly
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Platform availability of at least 99.95% in each calendar month in Section 9.1, and Exhibit B consistently lists the Platform Uptime target as ≥ 99.95%.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly excludes both scheduled maintenance windows and Force Majeure Events from uptime Downtime calculations in Section 9.1. Exhibit B also confirms these exclusions and specifies the scheduled-maintenance conditions, including 72 hours’ notice and a four-hour monthly limit.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the API latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Section 9.2 and consistently reflects that target in Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags latency as yellow-zone item (450 ms vs. product team's 400 ms preference)
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list identifies “Latency — p95 ≤ 450 ms” as Partially Resolved, expressly flags it as a yellow-zone caution, and states that Product Engineering prefers sub-400 ms for LendStream real-time decisioning.

criteria_results.title: F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 initial
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the initial contractual F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 during the Stabilization Period and requires F1 ≥ 0.92 for Go-Live acceptance. The prior 0.90 threshold is deleted.

criteria_results.title: F1 ramp mechanism to ≥ 0.94 after 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contractually requires F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day Stabilization Period following the October 1, 2025 Go-Live and increases the target to F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026 and thereafter. This ramp is reflected in Section 9.3 and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: SLA service credits capped at 20% of monthly fees ($40,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 inserts the required 20%/$40,000 monthly cap, but Section 9.4 also retains operative language stating a 30% monthly cap. This internal conflict means the agreement does not consistently set the cap exclusively at 20%/$40,000, despite Exhibit B using the correct amount.

criteria_results.title: Termination right for 3 consecutive months of SLA miss retained
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly retains Customer’s right to terminate if Vendor misses any SLA target—uptime, latency, or accuracy—for three consecutive calendar months, as stated in Section 9.5 and Exhibit B, Section 6.

criteria_results.title: New AI-output indemnity provision inserted
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 inserts Section 11.1A, “AI-Output Indemnification,” requiring Vendor to defend, indemnify, and hold Customer harmless from third-party claims alleging that Platform-generated outputs infringe or misappropriate IP rights or violate applicable law, including consumer-protection, fair-lending, financial-services, and privacy laws.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity carve-out for Customer modification or off-label use
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.1A expressly excludes claims caused by Customer’s modification of an output after receipt or Customer’s use outside the documented use case, satisfying the required carve-out.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope broadened to all intellectual property rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly broadens Section 11.1 beyond registered U.S. patents and copyrights. It covers all Intellectual Property Rights arising from Customer’s authorized use of the Platform, Base Model, Customer-Trained Adaptations, or outputs, including patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, moral rights, and analogous foreign-law rights worldwide.

criteria_results.title: Escrow of adapter weights plus training configuration and pipeline artifacts
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 requires escrow of fine-tuned adapter weights and all training configuration and pipeline artifacts needed to deploy, maintain, or redeploy them, while expressly excluding the Base Model source code and Vendor’s general proprietary training infrastructure.

criteria_results.title: Iron Mountain IPM as proposed escrow agent with NCC Group as acceptable alternative
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 names Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the proposed Escrow Agent and expressly states that NCC Group plc is an acceptable fallback if equivalent AI/ML escrow capability is confirmed. The updated issues list also reflects Iron Mountain as primary and NCC Group as the fallback.

criteria_results.title: Escrow release triggers include insolvency, material uncured breach (>60 days), and cessation of product support
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes all required escrow release triggers in Section 5A.3: Vendor insolvency or bankruptcy, a material breach remaining uncured for more than 60 days after notice, and cessation or announced discontinuation of Platform support.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance accepted at $5M per occurrence in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets Technology Errors & Omissions / Cyber Liability Insurance at $5,000,000 per occurrence (and $10,000,000 annual aggregate), expressly accepting Meridian’s current $5 million per-occurrence limit.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags Tech E&O as yellow-zone item (playbook prefers $10M for TCV > $5M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list flags Tech E&O at $5M per occurrence as a yellow-zone caution and expressly notes that the playbook prefers $10M for TCV above $5M, identifying the relevant TCV as $7.2M before implementation and usage.

criteria_results.title: Delaware governing law maintained in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 maintains Delaware governing law in Section 14.1, which states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. No other state's law is specified as governing law.

criteria_results.title: Delaware courts (Court of Chancery or U.S. District Court for D. Del.) as dispute forum
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.2 requires disputes to be resolved exclusively in the Delaware Court of Chancery, or if that court declines jurisdiction, the Delaware Superior Court or the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. It does not require arbitration or use a Massachusetts forum.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes CCPA service-provider certification language
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D, Section 3 expressly certifies that Vendor is a “service provider” as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), acting solely on Customer’s documented instructions, and includes restrictions on selling, sharing, retaining, using, or disclosing Customer Data consistent with CCPA/CPRA service-provider requirements.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes GLBA safeguards compliance
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses GLBA safeguards compliance. Exhibit D, Section 4 states that Vendor acknowledges Customer Data includes consumer NPPI subject to GLBA and agrees to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements. The agreement also references GLBA and its implementing regulations, including the FTC Safeguards Rule, in Section 6.3.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes 72-hour data breach notification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3’s DPA Section 8 requires Vendor to notify Customer in writing of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours after discovery or awareness.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes sub-processor management with prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3's DPA, Section 6, expressly states that Vendor may not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer's prior written consent. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes de-identification standards with statutory compliance and independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3’s DPA requires de-identified data to meet the CCPA statutory standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), include safeguards against re-identification, and be verified before use by an independent third-party assessor approved in writing by Customer. It therefore includes both required statutory compliance and independent verification.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes data return/deletion upon termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 addresses return and deletion upon termination in Exhibit D, Section 10, requiring Vendor to return or delete all Customer Data in accordance with Agreement Section 6.7 within 30 days of Customer’s written request and certify completion in writing. Agreement Section 6.7 provides further return/deletion details.

criteria_results.title: Issues list covers all 12 minimum negotiation point categories
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list expressly covers all 12 required categories: IP ownership/licensing (#5), liability cap (#6), data processing/de-identification (#8), uptime SLA (#1), latency SLA (#2), accuracy/F1 SLA (#3), SLA credits (#4), escrow (#13), AI-output indemnity (#9), IP indemnity scope (#10), Tech E&O insurance (#11), and governing law/dispute resolution (#12).

criteria_results.title: IP ownership/licensing categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “IP ownership / license structure” as “Partially Resolved” and explains that Meridian’s perpetual-license construct is accepted only if the portability, escrow, and non-assertion protections remain intact, indicating those provisions are not yet fully agreed.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the liability cap (Issue 6) as “Open,” reflecting that Draft 3 proposes a 1.5× annual-fee compromise that Meridian has not accepted. The criterion expressly permits either “Open” or “Partially Resolved,” and it is not marked fully resolved.

criteria_results.title: Data processing/de-identification categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes issue 8, “Data processing / CCPA service-provider / de-identification,” as “Partially Resolved” and explains that service-provider/processor status is retained while de-identification certification remains disputed.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA categorized as resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Uptime SLA — 99.95% monthly” as “Resolved” and retains the agreed exclusions for scheduled maintenance and Force Majeure.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the latency SLA as “Partially Resolved,” states that 450 ms is accepted as the contractual target, and notes that Product Engineering still prefers sub-400 ms performance.

criteria_results.title: Accuracy/F1 SLA categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Accuracy / F1 ramp — 0.92 to 0.94” as Open and states that Meridian has not agreed to the proposed contractual ramp.

criteria_results.title: SLA credits categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes SLA credits (Issue 4) as "Open," reflecting that the proposed 20% / $40,000 monthly cap has not been accepted by Meridian. This satisfies the criterion, which permits either "Open" or "Partially Resolved."

criteria_results.title: Escrow categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes escrow (Issue 13) as “Open,” noting that the scope and agent remain disputed. The criterion expressly permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open” and only fails if escrow is marked fully “Resolved.”

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes issue 9, “AI-output indemnity,” as “Open” and states that Meridian has provided no substantive response. The redline also labels the provision as open.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 10, “IP indemnity scope,” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not affirmatively accepted the broadened language.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance categorized as partially resolved with yellow-zone flag
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Insurance — Tech E&O $5M per occurrence” as “Partially Resolved” and expressly flags it as a “Yellow-zone caution.” The redline also includes a corresponding yellow-zone caution note.

criteria_results.title: Governing law/dispute resolution categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes issue 12, “Governing law / dispute resolution,” as “Open,” noting that TechNova retains Delaware law/courts while Meridian continues to request Massachusetts law and Boston AAA arbitration.

criteria_results.title: Draft 3 is redlined against Draft 2 as the base (not Draft 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly states that insertions and deletions are tracked against the clean, accepted Draft 2 base, and the agreement contains numerous tracked insertions and deletions. Nothing in the output indicates that Draft 1 or another document was used as the base.

criteria_results.title: Annual platform fee preserved at $2,400,000/yr
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the Annual Platform Fee at $2,400,000 per Contract Year in Section 4.1, invoiced as twelve monthly installments of $200,000. The updated issues list also confirms the $2.4 million annual fee is carried forward.

criteria_results.title: 3-year initial term preserved (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the three-year Initial Term. The Effective Date is July 1, 2025, and Section 13.1 states that the Initial Term expires on June 30, 2028; the updated issues list confirms the same dates.

criteria_results.title: Implementation fee preserved at $850,000 with 50/50 milestone split
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the $850,000 implementation fee and divides it into two equal $425,000 installments: the first upon execution of the Initial SOW and the second upon achievement of Go-Live. Exhibit A and the updated issues list confirm the same 50/50 milestone split.

criteria_results.title: Included API calls preserved at 40,000,000/yr with $0.012 overage
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves forty million (40,000,000) Included API Calls per Contract Year and an overage rate of $0.012 per API call in Section 4.3; the updated issues list also confirms these terms.

criteria_results.title: 180-day auto-renewal notice period preserved
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the 180-day auto-renewal notice period. Section 13.2 requires either party to provide notice of non-renewal at least 180 days before the current term expires, and the updated issues list confirms this term was carried forward.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes latency 450 ms is within playbook acceptable range but below preferred 400 ms
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies 450 ms as the accepted target, states that 500 ms is the Playbook’s outer acceptable threshold, and flags that Product Engineering prefers sub-400 ms for LendStream real-time decisioning. This provides the required acceptable-range and below-preference context.

criteria_results.title: Issues list recommends considering latency escalation at the May 19 joint call
criteria_results.reasoning: The latency issue entry expressly recommends revisiting the 450 ms target on the joint call planned for the week of May 19, while noting Product Engineering's preference for sub-400 ms performance.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags AI-output indemnity as fully open with no Meridian response
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list marks “AI-output indemnity” as “Open” and expressly states, “No substantive Meridian response,” satisfying the requirement to identify it as fully open and note Meridian’s lack of substantive response.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity (shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly states for Issue 9 (AI-output indemnity): “Playbook fallback: shared-risk framework with Meridian first-dollar defense / coverage and prompt remediation,” which satisfies the required fallback position.
